announcements.title: 21 Days of Prayer & Fasting begins this week
announcements.body: Nightly prayer at 7 PM on the stream, and a printed prayer guide at every branch. Join us as we consecrate the year.

announcements.title: Parking stewards at the Main Branch this Sunday
announcements.body: The north lot is resurfaced, so please arrive 15 minutes early and follow the stewards to the east entrance.

sermons.title: Overcoming in Christ
sermons.speaker: Dr. Tony Evans
sermons.summary: We are not fighting for victory, we are fighting from victory. Dr. Evans walks through what it means to be more than a conqueror — not a survivor of the battle, but somebody with spoils in their hands.
points: The overcomer's identity is settled at the cross, not at the altar
Overcoming is a posture, not an occasional event
Spoils belong to the one who keeps standing
questions: Where have I been fighting for a victory Christ already won?
What 'spoil' is God asking me to take hold of this week?

sermons.title: The Hope That Overcomes the World
sermons.speaker: Dr. John MacArthur
sermons.summary: Peace is not the absence of tribulation — Jesus promised the opposite. This message follows Christ's closing words to His disciples to show why a hope anchored outside this world cannot be shaken by it.
points: In the world you will have tribulation — expect it
Be of good cheer — the victory is already announced
Peace is a person before it is a feeling
questions: What tribulation have I been treating as a surprise?
How does my hope survive when circumstances don't change?

sermons.title: Overcoming the World
sermons.speaker: Dr. Voddie Baucham
sermons.summary: A careful walk through John's logic: faith is the victory, and faith is only as good as its object. Baucham presses the test of genuine belief — does your life prove what your lips profess?
points: Love for God and obedience are inseparable
Faith overcomes, not willpower
The witness of God is greater than the witness of men
questions: What evidence of new birth is present in my life?
Is my faith resting in a feeling or in the Son of God?

sermons.title: The Stages of Our Faith
sermons.speaker: Dr. Charles Stanley
sermons.summary: Faith grows in stages — seed, blade, ear, full grain — and God is patient in each one. A hopeful word for anyone who feels stuck between where they were and where they want to be.
points: Faith has seasons; God is Lord of all of them
Growth is often invisible before it is undeniable
Don't despise the stage you are in
questions: Which stage am I in right now?
Where am I tempted to rush what God is growing slowly?

sermons.title: The Priority of Prayer
sermons.speaker: Dr. Charles Stanley
sermons.summary: Jesus was busier than any of us and still left the crowd to pray. If the Son of God needed the secret place, what makes us think we can lead our lives without it?
points: A rising bell before a ringing phone
Jesus prayed before He chose, healed and travelled
The busier the season, the more pressing the altar
questions: What would change if my first fifteen minutes belonged to God?
What have I been deciding without prayer?

sermons.title: The Secret of Effectual Prayer
sermons.speaker: Pastor Adrian Rogers
sermons.summary: Fervent prayer is not loud prayer — it is prayer that has been in the presence of God. This message unpacks the conditions Scripture attaches to praying that avails much.
points: Righteousness matters more than vocabulary
Confession clears the channel
Prevailing prayer is sustained prayer
questions: Is there anything I need to confess before I ask again?
What request have I given up on too soon?

sermons.title: Prayer That Moves God
sermons.speaker: Dr. Charles Stanley
sermons.summary: Abraham bargaining at the edge of Sodom teaches us that God invites argument, repetition and holy boldness from His children. Prayer changes things because prayer changes us.
points: Intercession is standing in the gap for another
Boldness honours God's character
God's delays are not God's denials
questions: Who needs me to stand in the gap this week?
What would holy boldness look like in my praying?

sermons.title: Putting Prayer First
sermons.speaker: Dr. Charles Stanley
sermons.summary: A practical message on unbroken prayer — an attitude of dependence that runs underneath the whole day rather than a scheduled slot that rarely arrives.
points: Pray without ceasing is a posture, not a marathon
Short prayers released through the day
Gratitude keeps the conversation open
questions: What reminder could I set to return to prayer today?
What am I carrying that I have not yet handed over?

sermons.title: Building a Godly Home
sermons.speaker: Pastor Josh Howerton
sermons.summary: A wife's wisdom builds a house; her folly pulls it down with her own hands. Warm, practical teaching on the quiet power of a woman who fears the Lord — and the husband called to love her sacrificially.
points: Every home is being built or dismantled daily
Wisdom is a way of speaking and a way of waiting
The house of God begins in the house
questions: What am I building with my words this week?
Where does my home need repair prayer?

sermons.title: Marriage: A Covenant, Not a Contract
sermons.speaker: Dr. Tony Evans
sermons.summary: A contract is broken when terms are violated; a covenant is kept because God is witness. This message reframes marriage as a divine binding that survives the seasons it passes through.
points: Contracts negotiate, covenants covenant
God is a witness, not a bystander
You keep a covenant when you don't feel like it
questions: Have I treated my vows as terms or as worship?
What am I doing that a covenant-keeper would not do?

sermons.title: Marriage, Family and Work
sermons.speaker: Pastor Gary Hamrick
sermons.summary: A verse-by-verse walk through Paul's house rules: submission shaped by love, children raised in instruction, work done heartily as unto the Lord. Ordinariness is not the enemy of holiness.
points: All authority answers to Christ
Fathers provoke by absence or anger
Your desk is an altar when you work as unto Him
questions: Which relationship needs re-ordering this week?
How can I make my work an act of worship?

sermons.title: Raising a Godly Home in a Corrupt World
sermons.speaker: Bro. Zac Poonen
sermons.summary: Discipleship is not a programme that happens after school — it is the running commentary of a life lived with God in front of children. Faith is caught far more than it is taught.
points: Children learn what they live
Family worship should be normal, not ceremonial
Consistency is louder than curriculum
questions: What would my children say I love most?
What small family habit could we start this week?

sermons.title: Finding Your Purpose
sermons.speaker: Pastor Steven Furtick
sermons.summary: You are God's workmanship — the word is poiema, a poem. Purpose is not discovered by looking inward but by looking up and then walking forward in the ordinary things already in your hand.
points: You were created in Christ Jesus for good works
God doesn't need you to be impressive, just available
Purpose is walked out, not waited for
questions: What is already in my hand that God can use?
Where am I waiting for a calling instead of obeying today?

sermons.title: Finding Your Purpose in Life
sermons.speaker: Skip Heitzig
sermons.summary: Nehemiah heard a report, wept, prayed, and then asked the king for permission. A study in how a burden becomes a blueprint — the anatomy of a God-given assignment.
points: Purpose often begins with a burden you cannot shake
Prayer precedes planning
Provision follows the decision to build
questions: What report makes me weep?
What request have I not yet made?

sermons.title: How to Know the Purpose of Your Life
sermons.speaker: Dr. Myles Munroe
sermons.summary: A landmark message on the difference between a job, a career and a calling — and why your gift was never given for your own benefit alone. The cross is the model: potency poured out for others.
points: Purpose precedes your birth and outlives your death
Your gift makes room for you and serves others
Never exchange your assignment for a salary
questions: Whose lives would improve if I used my gift fully?
What am I trading my assignment for?

sermons.title: Grace Alone
sermons.speaker: Dr. Charles Stanley
sermons.summary: If grace is a gift, then no one can boast — and no one can be disqualified for lack of credentials. A freeing message for the performance-weary believer.
points: Grace excludes boasting and includes the undeserving
Faith is the hand that receives, not the price that pays
You cannot work for what was given
questions: Where am I still trying to earn God's approval?
What would rest look like for me this week?

sermons.title: The Transforming Grace of God
sermons.speaker: Dr. Charles Stanley
sermons.summary: Grace is not permission to sin; it is power to say no. The same grace that saves teaches us to deny ungodliness and to live soberly, righteously and godly in this present world.
points: Grace has appeared, to all men, and it teaches
Salvation and transformation are one package
The forgiven life is a different life
questions: What is grace teaching me to put down?
Where has grace become an excuse in my life?

sermons.title: The Gospel of the Grace of God
sermons.speaker: Dr. Charles Stanley
sermons.summary: Paul counted his own life dear only for the sake of finishing his course and the ministry of testifying to the gospel of the grace of God. What would it look like for that to be our single ambition?
points: The gospel is news, not advice
Grace is the content of the message
Finishing matters more than impressing
questions: What is my one thing?
Who has not yet heard this news from me?

sermons.title: Grace is God at Work
sermons.speaker: Pastor Louie Giglio
sermons.summary: God's strength does not meet us after our weakness is resolved — it is perfected in the middle of it. A message for anyone who thinks their cracks disqualify them from usefulness.
points: Grace shows up in weakness, not after it
Boasting in weakness is a discipline
God's power is made perfect, not slightly better
questions: What weakness have I been hiding instead of offering?
Where have I seen God work through my limits?

items.name: Amara O.
items.title: The scan came back clear
items.body: In March the doctors found a growth and gave us a date for surgery. Our small group began fasting on Tuesdays with us. Two weeks before the operation they repeated the scan and found nothing. Nothing. I have never cried like that in a hospital corridor — joy, not fear. God still heals.

items.name: Daniel & Rebekah M.
items.title: Our marriage came back from the edge
items.body: We sat in Pastor Michael's office certain we were done. Twelve years, two children, and nothing left but logistics. He asked us to try one thing: pray together out loud for six weeks. It was awkward for about four days. Then God met us in the awkwardness. We celebrate our anniversary again — properly.

items.name: Anonymous
items.title: Free after eleven years
items.body: I was bound to something I couldn't speak about for eleven years. I told one intercessor after a Friday service, expecting to be shamed. Instead she prayed with me until 1 a.m. That was fourteen months ago and I have not gone back once. If you are hiding, please — one honest conversation changes everything.

items.name: Priya S.
items.title: A job before the last payment left the account
items.body: My visa did not permit me to be unemployed for long. I applied for over ninety roles and heard nothing. The week my savings ran dry a stranger in this church forwarded my CV to her manager. I interviewed on Thursday and started on Monday. The salary was more than I had dared to ask for.

items.name: Joseph K.
items.title: My father gave his life to Christ at 78
items.body: I prayed for my father for twenty-six years. He mocked my faith, then tolerated it, then grew quiet about it. Last October he called me from the hospital and asked me to read him something from the Bible. We prayed together on speakerphone. He was gloriously saved at 78 and went home to Jesus four months later.

items.name: The Adekunle family
items.title: Our whole street came to the barbecue
items.body: We were terrified to host the summer barbecue on our street. Two families from church came to help set up, and we simply loved people — no agenda, no tracts, just food. Forty-one neighbours came. Eleven of them have since visited a service, and two are doing Next Steps with us.

items.name: Ruth N.
items.title: God in the night shift
items.body: I am a nurse and I was burning out quietly. Someone in the prayer team wrote me one handwritten card a month — just scripture and 'we are praying for you'. Fourteen cards later I finished my residency. You will never know the ministry of your car dashboard and a stamp.

items.name: Michael T.
items.title: The debt snowball is gone
items.body: Six years ago we were carrying $48,000 of consumer debt. We joined the financial freedom class, stopped pretending, and started giving even while we were paying it down. Last month we made the final payment. I have the screenshot on my phone and I show it to strangers.

visitExpect.title: A greeter at the door
visitExpect.text: Someone will meet you, show you where to go and answer any question you have — including where the toilets are.

visitExpect.title: About two hours
visitExpect.text: Worship and prayer, a Bible message, and a short time of ministry at the altar. Leave whenever you need to.

visitExpect.title: Children are welcome
visitExpect.text: Kingdom Kids runs during both Sunday services with secure check-in. Children are also welcome to stay with you.

visitExpect.title: Nothing to pay
visitExpect.text: There is no entry fee and no pressure to give. An offering basket is passed for those who want to participate.

visitExpect.title: Dress as you are
visitExpect.text: Some wear suits, some wear jeans. God looks at the heart and so do we.

visitExpect.title: Prayer if you want it
visitExpect.text: At the end of every service our pastors pray with anyone who comes forward — quietly, briefly and without fuss.
